title: Getting Started
text: wrapbox package provides tools extracting stream networks delineating watersheds using flow direction flow accumulation rasters. wrapper package whitebox (see package website). vignette demonstrates : Extract stream networks raster grids flow accumulation data. Convert stream grids vector stream networks. Delineate unnested nested watersheds using outlet locations. example data include D8 flow direction raster (dir.tif; flow directions coded according ArcGIS) upstream area raster (upa.tif), provided package. raster layers derived MeritHydro developed Yamazaki et al.

title: Getting Started
text: First, load required packages example raster layers. example rasters distributed raster/ directory. Use system.file() locate installing package. Importantly, however, flow direction layer must converted Whitebox D8 scheme source data coded according ArcGIS scheme; otherwise, Whitebox tools function properly return erroneous outputs. wrapbox::arc2d8() function performs conversion. Inspect raster properties. flow direction raster (f_dir) represents direction water flow cell, whereas flow accumulation raster (f_acc) represents upstream contributing area. layers must use compatible spatial extents, resolutions, coordinate reference systems. Visualize raster layers tidyterra::geom_spatraster() function:
code: pacman::p_load(   tidyverse,   wrapbox,   sf,   terra,   tidyterra ) ## flow direction layer dir_file <- system.file(   "raster", "dir.tif",   package = "wrapbox" )  ## flow accumulation layer upa_file <- system.file(   "raster", "upa.tif",   package = "wrapbox" )  f_dir <- terra::rast(dir_file) f_acc <- terra::rast(upa_file) f_dir <- arc2d8(f_dir) f_dir #> class       : SpatRaster #> size        : 738, 859, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr) #> resolution  : 0.0008333333, 0.0008333333  (x, y) #> extent      : -81.17292, -80.45708, 35.57375, 36.18875  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) #> coord. ref. : lon/lat WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) #> source(s)   : memory #> varname     : dir #> name        : n35w085_dir #> min value   :           1 #> max value   :         128 f_acc #> class       : SpatRaster #> size        : 738, 859, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr) #> resolution  : 0.0008333333, 0.0008333333  (x, y) #> extent      : -81.17292, -80.45708, 35.57375, 36.18875  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) #> coord. ref. : lon/lat WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) #> source      : upa.tif #> name        : n35w085_upa #> min value   :    0.006923 #> max value   : 6353.152832 ## flow direction ggplot() +   geom_spatraster(data = f_dir) #> <SpatRaster> resampled to 500528 cells. ## flow accumulation ggplot() +   geom_spatraster(data = f_acc) #> <SpatRaster> resampled to 500528 cells.

what: 2.1. Extract streams as a raster grid
title: Getting Started
text: Stream networks can extracted applying threshold flow accumulation raster. flow2grid() function uses WhiteboxTools identify cells whose upstream contributing area exceeds specified threshold. threshold determines minimum upstream contributing area cell considered operational “stream.” Smaller thresholds generally produce denser networks, whereas larger thresholds retain larger streams. output argument determines destination output file – although used tempfile(fileext = ".tif") example, users may specify appropriate location repository. Note: threshold uses units input flow accumulation raster. Adjust according spatial resolution units data. Visualize extracted stream grid.
code: # Define the minimum upstream contributing area threshold <- 100  # Extract stream grid str_grid <- flow2grid(   f_acc = f_acc,   threshold = threshold,   output = tempfile(fileext = ".tif") ) ggplot() +   geom_spatraster(data = str_grid) #> <SpatRaster> resampled to 500528 cells.

what: 2.2. Convert stream grids into vector networks
title: Getting Started
text: Stream grids can converted vector lines using grid2stream(). function uses flow direction raster extracted stream grid reconstruct stream network. Please ensure flow direction layer conforms formatting requirements Whitebox tools (see 1. Load example data). resulting object sf line layer, visualization can done geom_sf().  optional output path can supplied save vector network.
code: str_vec <- grid2stream(   f_dir = f_dir,   str_grid = str_grid ) ggplot() +   geom_sf(data = str_vec) str_vec <- grid2stream(   f_dir = f_dir,   str_grid = str_grid,   output = "streams.gpkg" )

title: Getting Started
text: Watershed delineation requires outlet locations flow direction raster. Outlet locations placed stream network. default, wsd_unnested() wsd_nested() snap outlet points nearest stream cells delineating watersheds.

title: Getting Started
text: demonstration, use sf layer outlet points. Like raster data, example data distributed vector/ directory. Use system.file() locate .
code: ## load outlet data file outlet_file <- system.file(   "vector", "outlet.rds",   package = "wrapbox" )  ## load data outlet <- readRDS(outlet_file)     ## inspect ggplot() +   geom_sf(data = str_vec) +   geom_sf(data = outlet,           color = "red")

title: Getting Started
text: wsd_unnested() function delineates independent watersheds supplied outlet locations. resulting object sf polygon layer, one watershed polygon per outlet. snap_dist argument specifies maximum distance snapping outlet locations stream network, using map units input raster. Since resulting watershed polygons overlapped one another, watershed polygon upstream site deeper color (alpha less 1).
code: wsd <- wsd_unnested(   outlet = outlet,   id_col = "id",   f_dir = f_dir,   str_grid = str_grid,   snap = TRUE,   snap_dist = 5 ) #> Saving temporary files... #> Snap outlet points to the nearest stream grid... #> Delineate watersheds... #> Vectorize raster watersheds... #> Reading layer `outlet_snap' from data source  #>   `C:\Users\a_terui\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpQrlGfb\wsd_18276_476417426b02\outlet_snap.shp'  #>   using driver `ESRI Shapefile' #> Simple feature collection with 2 features and 2 fields #> Geometry type: POINT #> Dimension:     XY #> Bounding box:  xmin: -80.80833 ymin: 35.78167 xmax: -80.5175 ymax: 36.03083 #> Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84 #> Registered S3 method overwritten by 'stars': #>   method                  from #>   st_interpolate_aw.stars sf ggplot() +   geom_sf(data = wsd,           fill = "blue",           alpha = 0.1) +   geom_sf(data = str_vec) +   geom_sf(data = outlet,           color = "red")

title: Getting Started
text: Nested watersheds (.e., watersheds split multiple polygons outlet point) can delineated using wsd_nested(). resulting watershed polygons represent nested, non-overlapping drainage areas associated respective outlet locations. polygons overlap, plotting transparent fills produce color variation.
code: wsd_nested <- wsd_nested(   outlet = outlet,   id_col = "id",   f_dir = f_dir,   str_grid = str_grid,   snap = TRUE,   snap_dist = 5 ) #> Saving temporary files... #> Snap outlet points to the nearest stream grid... #> Delineate watersheds... #> Vectorize raster watersheds... #> Reading layer `outlet_snap' from data source  #>   `C:\Users\a_terui\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpQrlGfb\wsd_18276_476433865a24\outlet_snap.shp'  #>   using driver `ESRI Shapefile' #> Simple feature collection with 2 features and 2 fields #> Geometry type: POINT #> Dimension:     XY #> Bounding box:  xmin: -80.80833 ymin: 35.78167 xmax: -80.5175 ymax: 36.03083 #> Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84 ggplot() +   geom_sf(data = wsd_nested,           fill = "blue",           alpha = 0.1) +   geom_sf(data = str_vec) +   geom_sf(data = outlet,           color = "red")
